    press key 44 <AB01> -> 'y'
    wdotool key 52                             (keycodes)
    wdotool type 'y'                           (characters)

    press key 21 <AD06> -> 'z'
    wdotool key 29                             (keycodes)
    wdotool type 'z'                           (characters)
'@' -- 1 press on German
    press key 16 <AD01> with level3 (key 100 <RALT>, ISO_Level3_Shift) -> '@'
    wdotool key 108+24                         (keycodes)
    wdotool type '@'                           (characters)

### rc=0
### wxrandr --output Virtual-2 --mode 1680x1050
xrandr: Hyprland accepted the live `keyword monitor` and did not apply it, so the layout went into /home/test/.config/hypr/w11-monitors.conf and the config was reloaded (the whole config is re-read: runtime `hyprctl keyword`s set since login are reset)
xrandr: those rules stay in /home/test/.config/hypr/w11-monitors.conf, with or without --persistent: Hyprland re-reads a file it sources as soon as it changes, so taking them back out puts the head straight back at its preferred mode (measured on Hyprland 0.56.2, 2026-09-11). Delete that file, or the `source =` line hyprland.conf carries for it, to undo this layout

w11: wdotool, wwmctl, wxprop, wxrandr, warandr and wmirror are on PATH.

  * On GNOME, the window commands need the bridge extension, and gnome-shell
    only scans extension directories at login: LOG OUT AND BACK IN ONCE.

    60-w11-uinput.rules).  Anyone who can open it can type as you.

    pacman -S xdotool wmctrl xorg-xprop xorg-xrandr
